papers.title: PD-(L)1×VEGF bispecific antibodies in solid tumors: clinical trial updates from ASCO 2026
papers.authors: Wang Z, Guo C, Yuan X, Guo Q, Zhang R, Chen Z
papers.abstract: PD-(L)1×VEGF bispecific antibodies integrate immune checkpoint blockade and VEGF inhibition within a single molecule, offering a potential strategy to overcome angiogenesis-associated immune resistance. At the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting, the randomized phase 3 HARMONi-6 trial demonstrated an overall survival benefit with ivonescimab plus chemotherapy over tislelizumab plus chemotherapy in previously untreated advanced squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), extending survival evidence to an active PD-1-based first-line comparator. Exploratory phase 2 studies of pumitamig, SSGJ-707, and HB0025 reported encouraging activity in first-line NSCLC, while phase 1 and 2 studies of IMM2510 and ivonescimab-based regimens suggested activity after prior immunotherapy. Smaller exploratory studies also reported activity in perioperative head and neck cancer, colorectal cancer, endometrial cancer, and mucosal melanoma. Collectively, these findings highlight the clinical potential of PD-(L)1×VEGF bispecific antibodies, with the strongest evidence in first-line squamous NSCLC and broader applications remaining hypothesis-generating. Future development should prioritize predictive biomarkers, resistance mechanisms, optimal treatment sequencing, and careful assessment of immune-related and VEGF-associated toxicities.

papers.title: Liposomal irinotecan and capecitabine plus bevacizumab as second-line therapy in metastatic colorectal cancer: A multicenter, single-arm study
papers.authors: Su D, Li C, Zheng T, Tang J, Wang G, Xu H
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liposomal irinotecan, characterized by its favorable pharmacologic properties and reduced systemic toxicity compared to irinotecan, has demonstrated superior therapeutic potential. This multicenter, single-arm study was conducted to evaluate the efficacy and safety of liposomal irinotecan, capecitabine, and bevacizumab as a second-line treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC).
METHODS: Patients with histologically confirmed mCRC who had progressed following first-line oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy were enrolled in this study. The treatment regimen was liposomal irinotecan (70 mg/m2, d1), capecitabine (1000 mg/m2, twice daily, d1-10), and bevacizumab (5 mg/kg, d1). The primary endpoint was progression-free survival. Secondary endpoints included objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, overall survival, and safety.
RESULTS: Between March 2024 and July 2024, 63 patients were enrolled, with a median age of 60.0 years (range: 37.0-79.0). Among the patients who received at least one tumor assessment, the objective response rate and disease control rate were 22.9% (11/48; 95% CI, 12.0-37.3) and 89.6% (43/48; 95% CI, 77.3-96.5), respectively. With a median follow-up of 16.2 months (range: 0.5-28.5), the median progression-free survival was 8.1 months (95% CI, 7.3-8.9), and the median overall survival was 19.5 months (95% CI, 15.2-23.8). The most common grade 3 to 4 adverse events were diarrhea (12.7%), neutropenia (11.1%), and fatigue (6.3%).
CONCLUSIONS: The combination of liposomal irinotecan, capecitabine, and bevacizumab demonstrated promising antitumor activity and a manageable safety profile in patients with mCRC who had failed first-line oxaliplatin-based therapy. These results suggested that this regimen is a clinically feasible second-line treatment option for mCRC.

papers.title: Operative efficiency and short-term outcomes of da Vinci 5 versus da Vinci Xi in robotic rectal cancer surgery: an overlap-weighted cohort study with an exploratory case insights analysis
papers.authors: Ishiyama Y, Hirano Y, Kitano Y, Yamazaki N, Sakai Y, Nakanishi A
papers.abstract: The da Vinci 5 introduces changes in operative workflow and instrument control, but its comparative performance in rectal cancer surgery remains uncertain. We compared operative efficiency and short-term outcomes after platform introduction and explored platform-derived intraoperative measurements. This retrospective single-center study included 202 patients undergoing robot-assisted rectal cancer surgery from July 2025 to September 2026 (Xi, n = 109; da Vinci 5, n = 93). Propensity-score overlap weighting addressed measured differences. The primary outcome was total operative time. HC3 inference was checked using 2,000 bootstrap replicates with propensity-score re-estimation. Retrieved Case Insights records were summarized descriptively. The adjusted difference in total operative time was - 6.9 min (HC3 95% confidence interval [CI], - 24.4 to 10.6; P = 0.439); the bootstrap 95% CI was - 21.8 to 7.8 min. The adjusted risk difference for Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ II complications was - 9.4% points (HC3 95% CI, - 19.8 to 0.9; P = 0.074). Margin positivity occurred in only three patients and was reported descriptively. Inference for postoperative hospital stay depended on the variance method. We did not detect a statistically clear reduction in total operative time after the introduction of the da Vinci 5. Secondary outcomes remain exploratory. Exploratory Case Insights analysis provided descriptive information on instrument-tip force and surgical workflow, warranting further prospective validation of their clinical relevance.

papers.title: Multidrug-resistant monophasic Salmonella Typhimurium ST34 strain producing bla NDM-5 carbapenemase isolated from a patient with rectal cancer in Hainan, China: comprehensive whole genome dissection of antibiotic resistance and virulence determinants
papers.journal_full: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.authors: Zhong S, Xing L, Wang L, Wang C, Fu X, Xu L
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Here, we report the identification and comprehensive whole-genome characterization of a New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase 5 (bla NDM-5)-producing multidrug-resistant (MDR) monophasic Salmonella Typhimurium ST34 strain SYA001 from an immunocompromised rectal cancer patient. Monophasic Salmonella Typhimurium (Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar 1,4,[5],12:i:-) is one of the leading causative agents of foodborne gastroenteritis and hospitalization worldwide, and the rapid emergence and spread of carbapenem-resistant strains have severely compromised clinical treatment and posed a major threat to public health.
METHODS: In this study, a series of standardized phenotypic assays were performed to characterize the microbiological, biochemical, and antimicrobial resistance profiles of strain SYA001. Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS), biochemical identification, and slide agglutination serotyping were used for species and serotype confirmation. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using the VITEK 2 compact system, and six types of carbapenemases were screened via a colloidal gold immunochromatographic assay. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on the DNBSEQ-T7 platform, and a comprehensive bioinformatics pipeline was applied to dissect the genomic structure, phylogenetic characteristics, antibiotic resistance determinants, plasmid profiles, prophage regions, Salmonella pathogenicity islands (SPIs), and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network of the strain.
RESULTS: Our results confirmed that SYA001 is a serovar 1,4,[5],12:i:- monophasic Salmonella Typhimurium belonging to the globally epidemic ST34 clone. The strain exhibited an MDR phenotype, with resistance to 7 classes of antibiotics including carbapenems, cephalosporins, and aminoglycosides, and was only susceptible to aztreonam, amikacin, tigecycline, and colistin. Genomic analysis identified the core carbapenem resistance gene bla NDM-5, along with multiple coexisting resistance genes including bla OXA-10, qnrS1, tet(A), sul2, and sul3 and so on. Four plasmid replicons (IncHI2, IncHI2A, IncQ1, p0111), 15 prophage regions, and a complete set of virulence-related SPIs (SPI-1 to SPI-5,SPI-9, SPI-13, SPI-14) were detected. PPI network analysis revealed AcrA as the core hub of the efflux-mediated resistance regulatory network.
CONCLUSION: This study provides genomic insights into bla NDM-5-producing MDR monophasic Salmonella. Typhimurium from an immunocompromised rectal cancer patient, supplements clinical surveillance data of carbapenem-resistant Salmonella in Hainan.

papers.title: Targeting the gut-tumor axis: probiotic therapy as an adjunct strategy in colorectal cancer treatment
papers.journal_full: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.authors: Li H, Hou C, Pan Y
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a multifactorial disease driven by interactions among host genetics, immune dysregulation, environmental factors, and gut microbiota. The gut-tumor axis regulates CRC progression through inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress, epithelial barrier disruption, and immune imbalance. Probiotic-derived metabolites act as bioactive molecules capable of restoring host-microbiome homeostasis and modulating tumor-associated pathways.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate probiotic metabolites as adjunct therapeutic agents in CRC using integrative multi-omics analysis and in vitro validation.
METHODS: A systems biology approach integrating network pharmacology, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and microbiome profiling was applied. Twelve probiotic metabolites yielded 428 predicted targets, with 162 overlapping CRC-associated genes. CRC cell lines (HCT116, HT-29, Caco-2, SW480) were treated and analyzed for viability, apoptosis, gene/protein expression, cytokines, metabolites, and microbial composition.
RESULTS: Sodium butyrate (5 mM) reduced cell viability by 35.5-42.3% (p < 0.001) and increased apoptosis from 8.6% to 32.4%, reaching 41.2% when combined with indole-3-acetic acid (IAA, 100 μM), suggesting a synergistic pro-apoptotic effect. RNA-seq identified 1,248 DEGs, with upregulation of BAX and CASP3 (log2FC +1.8 to +2.3) and downregulation of IL6, TNF, and NFKB1 (-1.5 to -2.1). Proteomics revealed 412 differentially expressed proteins, including downregulation of AKT1 (-1.6-fold), MAPK1 (-1.4-fold), and EGFR (-1.3-fold), and upregulation of CASP3 (+1.7-fold) and BAX (+1.5-fold). Cytokines IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β decreased by 48.2%, 44.7%, and 39.5%, respectively, while IL-10 increased by 26.3%. Metabolomics showed a 2.8-fold increase in butyrate and ~35% reduction in oxidative stress. Microbiome diversity improved (Shannon index 2.8-3.6).
CONCLUSION: Probiotic-derived metabolites modulate NF-κB, PI3K-Akt, MAPK, and apoptosis pathways, supporting their potential role as adjunct therapeutic agents in CRC management.

papers.title: Program maturation across 364 robotic colorectal procedures: postoperative recovery, operative efficiency, and major morbidity
papers.authors: Monsellato I, Palucci M, Giannone F, Marotta F, Alagia M, Lodin M
papers.abstract: Robotic colorectal learning-curve studies commonly define proficiency using operative time or cumulative-sum thresholds, which may not capture maturation of a heterogeneous program. In this retrospective longitudinal cohort, we analyzed 364 consecutive robotic colorectal procedures from a single-surgeon, single-center program using prior global robotic colorectal experience as a continuous exposure. Principal clinical outcomes were postoperative length of stay (LOS) and major morbidity (Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher); operative duration was the principal process/efficiency outcome. Multivariable log-linear models adjusted for procedure family, robotic platform, associated procedures, age, and American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class; major morbidity was analyzed with Firth penalized logistic regression. Each doubling of (1 + prior experience) was associated with 5.1% shorter LOS (95% CI 2.2%-7.9% shorter; p < 0.001) and 5.3% shorter operative duration (95% CI 3.3%-7.4% shorter; p < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed no evidence of LOS non-linearity (p = 0.621) but significant non-linearity for operative duration (p < 0.001). Major morbidity occurred in 15/364 procedures (4.1%); the adjusted Firth odds ratio was 1.48 per experience doubling (95% profile-likelihood CI 0.84-3.64; p = 0.208). Because cumulative experience and calendar time were essentially collinear, estimates represent longitudinal program maturation rather than an isolated causal surgeon-experience effect. Greater cumulative experience was associated with shorter LOS and operative duration, but the LOS association should be interpreted as a program-level signal that may also reflect evolving perioperative care; major morbidity remained uncommon but imprecisely estimated longitudinally.

papers.title: Pulmonary metastasectomy in solid tumors: a single-center experience at a tertiary referral center in the Middle East
papers.authors: Ghanayem M, Jalil R, Al Matairi A, El-Edwan A, Yousef L, Aburabie S
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advances in systemic therapy, pulmonary metastasectomy remains a key option for selected patients with metastatic solid tumors, offering long-term survival. Prognosis is influenced by many factors including disease-free interval and metastatic burden. This study evaluates survival outcomes and prognostic factors in a mixed-tumor cohort from a Middle Eastern tertiary cancer center.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included all patients who underwent pulmonary metastasectomy for solid tumors at King Hussein Cancer Center between October 2014 and December 2024. Demographic, clinical, imaging, surgical, pathological, and follow-up data were collected from electronic medical records. Overall survival (OS) and pulmonary recurrence-free survival (P-RFS) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and prognostic factors were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. Analyses were performed using SPSS version 27.
RESULTS: A total of 236 patients underwent 371 procedures. The mean follow-up was 31.9 months (95% CI:28.3-35.3). Median OS was 3.99 years (95% CI:2.69-5.28), with a 5-year OS rate of 42.0%. Mean P-RFS was 6.81 years (95% CI: 6.16-7.46), with the median not reached. On univariable analysis, worse OS was associated with metastatic lesion size ≥ 3 cm, bilateral metastases, thoracotomy, longer hospital stay, and increased tumor burden. R0 resection and DFI ≥ 12 months were protective. In multivariable analysis, independent predictors of worse OS were metastatic lesion size ≥ 3 cm (HR: 1.827, p = 0.015) and DFI < 12 months (HR for ≥ 12 months: 0.515, p = 0.002). Patients with colorectal cancer demonstrated numerically longer overall survival and lower pulmonary recurrence rates than patients with sarcoma (5-year OS: 44.8% vs. 32.2%; pulmonary recurrence: 18.8% vs. 34.4%). However, tumor type was not significantly associated with overall survival in univariable Cox regression analysis.
CONCLUSION: Pulmonary metastasectomy is an important treatment option for patients with lung metastasis from different solid tumors that provides durable long-term and pulmonary recurrence-free survival in appropriately selected patients. Longer DFI and smaller metastatic lesion size independently predict improved outcomes.

papers.title: Multi-omics Profiling of Post-translational Modifications in RNA-binding Proteins in Colorectal Cancer
papers.authors: Dong Y, Ruan W, Qi D, Tang D, Dai Y, Zhang W
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) play a pivotal role in regulating RNA-binding proteins (RBPs), which are crucial in the progression of colorectal cancer (CRC). This study aims to explore the role of PTMs in modulating RBPs and their implications for CRC pathogenesis.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We characterized phosphorylation, ubiquitination, and malonylation of RBPs in CRC using previously generated post-translational multi-omics datasets from paired CRC and adjacent non-tumor tissues in our previous studies. Functional enrichment analysis was conducted to identify pathways associated with RBPs carrying different PTMs in CRC. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were generated using STRING, and hub genes were identified with the Cytoscape plugin CytoHubba. We also investigated the intersection of RBPs with distinct PTMs and evaluated the expression and prognostic relevance of FLNA (filamin A).
RESULTS: Our findings revealed aberrant PTMs of RBPs in CRC, with ubiquitination sites showing the most frequent alterations, followed by phosphorylation, while malonylation exhibited the fewest changes. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that these PTMs contribute to distinct biological processes, including RNA metabolism, protein synthesis, and translation regulation. PPI network analysis showed that RBPs with different PTMs were interconnected in complex networks, identifying several potential RBPs closely related to CRC. Notably, FLNA emerged as a unique RBP modified by all three PTMs. FLNA mRNA and protein abundance were reduced in CRC, and phosphorylation of FLNA at S2319 was also decreased. Higher FLNA expression was associated with worse overall survival. FLNA-associated genes were enriched in pathways related to epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and KRAS signaling.
CONCLUSION: Multi-PTM profiling revealed distinct and convergent modification patterns among CRC-associated RBPs. FLNA emerged as a potential multi-PTM candidate associated with CRC-related molecular and clinical features. These findings provide a framework for further investigating the biological relevance of PTM-regulated RBPs and their potential implications for the development of molecularly targeted strategies in CRC.
